claims.statement: The Python worker is a sidecar launched and supervised by the Rust host as `python -m galpi_worker <command>` with the worker root on PYTHONPATH; the host picks the interpreter per engine (pinned WhisperX venv vs isolated Qwen3 venv) and sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE for Qwen3 transcription so it loads only from the prepared cache.

The worker CLI has exactly three subcommands: `prepare` (--manifest, --engine-bin, --engine), `transcribe` (--input, --output, optional --asr-context, --engine, mutually exclusive --num-speakers / --speaker-range MIN MAX), and `refine` (--transcript, --output, optional --background, --participants, --glossary, --model, --meeting-date).

Exit codes are a host contract: 0 on success, 2 for INVALID_INPUT, 1 for ENGINE_ERROR, and every abnormal exit emits exactly one protocol error event before dying — `main()` maps InvalidInput to INVALID_INPUT and a catch-all handler to ENGINE_ERROR because an unlisted exception type would otherwise die silently on stderr.

InvalidInput subclasses ValueError so existing callers keep working while `__main__` can distinguish Galpi's own input validation (exit 2) from a ValueError raised deep inside a model library, which is an engine failure (exit 1).

stdout is machine-readable protocol only: EventWriter in protocol.py is the sole writer, emitting one flushed JSON object per event with protocol v: 1, a monotonically increasing seq, and a type, guarded by a thread lock so concurrent map-phase emitters keep seq monotonic and never interleave mid-line; print/tqdm/logging handlers on stdout outside EventWriter are forbidden.

The entire pipeline runs inside `with redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)` in main() so dependency prints land on stderr instead of the protocol stream; a pure contract test prints under redirect_stdout beside an EventWriter.emit and asserts only the structured event reached the protocol.

The purity boundary keeps core.py, artifacts.py, the minutes_* modules, assistant_stream.py, protocol.py, and runtime.py free of ML-stack module-scope imports: Torch, WhisperX, pyannote, MLX, and imageio-ffmpeg are imported inside runtime functions, so package import and the stdlib unittest suite (run via `bun run check:worker` with `unittest discover`) work on a bare interpreter with no ML environment installed.

The worker is typed under strict basedpyright scoped to `worker` with stubPath `worker/stubs`, where hand-written .pyi stubs cover whisperx, pyannote.audio, torchaudio, and huggingface_hub; untyped library payloads are converted with explicit casts into local TypedDict contracts (Segment, Transcription, WordSpan, SpeakerTurn), and stubs must not be weakened merely to hide an installed-library mismatch.

engine.transcribe() is a one-line router on the --engine value: `qwen3` lazily imports and calls transcribe_qwen3 (MLX Qwen3-ASR-1.7B + ForcedAligner on Metal GPU with 8-bit weights), otherwise it calls transcribe_whisperx (faster-whisper large-v3-turbo via WhisperX/CTranslate2).

The bundled CLI's argparse default for --engine is `whisperx`, but the product default is the opposite: the Rust EnginePreset defaults to Qwen3 and the transcription adapter always passes --engine explicitly, so the CLI default never decides engine selection in production.

ASR deliberately stays on CTranslate2 CPU int8: transcribe_whisperx loads large-v3-turbo with device 'cpu', compute_type 'int8', language 'ko', batch size 8, no_speech_threshold 0.75, condition_on_previous_text False, and VAD onset/offset 0.6/0.4; moving ASR to MPS is an explicit anti-pattern.

Alignment and diarization prefer MPS (select_torch_device returns 'mps' when torch.backends.mps.is_available(), else 'cpu') and wrap their work in exactly one retry: on MPS failure the worker emits a log event explaining the CPU fallback and re-runs on CPU, with no additional retries, and on a CPU-only machine the failure propagates; prepare mirrors the same fallback and records the devices each stage landed on in the manifest.

Both engines share the same surrounding pipeline — speaker-hint validation, ffmpeg decode, pyannote speaker-diarization-community-1, filter_segments, and an identical published artifact set (SRT, speaker text, checkpoint) — differing only in the ASR core.

Each engine writes an `engine` tag into the `<name>.aligned.v2.json` checkpoint it publishes, and each only reuses a checkpoint carrying its own tag (WhisperX accepts None from pre-tag files or 'whisperx'; Qwen3 requires exactly 'qwen3'), preventing a run that switched presets from reading word timings produced by the other stack.
Reusing an existing checkpoint skips only ASR and alignment; diarization, filtering, and output publication always run, because the speaker hint changes far more often than the audio does.

Speaker hints map onto diarization directly — --num-speakers N to num_speakers=N, --speaker-range MIN MAX to min_speakers/max_speakers, no flag to automatic — and validate_speaker_hint rejects zero/negative counts and inverted ranges as InvalidInput before any model work starts.

The Qwen3 chunking constants (CHUNK_TARGET_SECONDS 25, CHUNK_MAX_SECONDS 30, cutting at the latest ffmpeg-silencedetect midpoint with -35dB floor and 0.6s minimum, hard cut at the max only when no usable silence exists) exist to keep chunks at or under the 30s limit at which mlx-qwen3-asr re-splits at an energy minimum that can land mid-word — Galpi's silence-aligned boundary is the one that survives — so changes to them are pipeline-behavior changes, and a test pins CHUNK_MAX_SECONDS <= 30.

Every Qwen3 input is decoded through the bundled ffmpeg binary (imageio-ffmpeg's) into 16 kHz mono WAV inside a temporary directory, because the stack's libsndfile decoder rejects compressed containers (m4a/AAC, mov); duration is read from the wave header without loading samples.

The Qwen3 ASR pass loads mlx_qwen3_asr.Session from the converted cache directory `<HF_HOME parent>/mlx/qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit` (a missing weights.safetensors raises a RuntimeError meaning prepare was skipped), transcribes silence-aligned sample slices per chunk with language='Korean' and return_timestamps=True, offsets chunk-local word timestamps onto the meeting clock, logs a chunk that stops for any reason other than finishing its text (length/repetition leave a visible hole), and releases the MLX and torch MPS caches before diarization loads.

build_word_spans lays the model's punctuated text over the aligner's words using the aligner's own matchable-character rule (Unicode letters/numbers plus apostrophes) and appends text the aligner never reached to the last span rather than dropping it; group_word_spans then merges timed words into speaker-labelled segments breaking at terminal punctuation only when whitespace follows (so '3.14' survives), at a speaker change, after a >=0.8s pause, or past 12s of speech — the speaker break keeps one unpunctuated stretch from collapsing several people into whoever spoke longest.

Qwen3 diarization uses pyannote.audio Pipeline.from_pretrained with the shared community-1 model and reads exclusive_speaker_diarization (dropping overlapping speech, which maps cleaner onto ASR segments); each word takes the turn covering most of it, or the nearest turn when diarization's trimming left it uncovered.

ASR biasing context is a cross-language wire contract: the Rust host serializes glossary terms, participant names, and spoken aliases as one JSON object ({terms, names, aliases}) into a 0600 temp file passed as --asr-context, and the worker's parse_asr_context trims entries, drops non-strings, and rejects malformed payloads with TypeError.

WhisperX consumes ASR context by packing terms > names > aliases into the model's hotwords option: entries are deduplicated, packed first-fit under ASR_HOTWORDS_CHAR_BUDGET = 200 characters (the hotwords slot keeps roughly the first 223 prompt tokens and Korean syllables average about one token each), and whole entries drop once the budget runs out rather than being cut mid-word.

Qwen3 consumes ASR context as a freeform Korean hint (domain terms / attendee names / aliases sections) truncated to BIAS_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET = 500 characters, because the hotword slot is finite and a runaway roster would crowd out the audio.

should_filter_segment removes three failure families before anything is written: known Korean hallucination phrases via regex, single-token repetition loops (>=6 tokens with one token covering >=80% — the Whisper silence failure confidence rules never catch), and phrase loops (a repeated 2-4 token n-gram covering >=60% of a >=8-token segment); filter_segments additionally drops tail noise after a >=120s silence beyond the audio's midpoint (low avg_logprob or ultra-short high-rate speech).

All outputs are written atomically via a sibling .tmp file followed by Path.replace/os.replace — the checkpoint (write_json_atomic), the SRT and speaker-text pair (write_outputs_atomic), refinement output, the prepare manifest, and the converted MLX weights — and the final artifact names `.aligned.v2.json`, `.srt`, and `_화자별.txt` are external behavior that must never be renamed.

Both engines finish transcription by emitting a `completed` event carrying the srt, txt, and checkpoint paths plus kept/filtered segment counts, which is the payload the Rust adapter maps into CompletedTranscription (an empty checkpoint string meaning no checkpoint).

prepare_models links the imageio-ffmpeg binary into --engine-bin (symlink, falling back to a copy), then warms the selected engine's models once each and writes the manifest JSON atomically (protocol: 1, package versions, model ids, per-stage devices) followed by a `prepared` event; the WhisperX warmup applies the same single MPS-to-CPU fallback per stage.

Qwen3 prepare snapshot-downloads Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B and Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B concurrently (two workers, DownloadReporter summing tqdm bytes onto the 10-40% band at one update per second), then converts the ASR snapshot into 8-bit group-64 MLX weights in a `<name>.partial` staging directory that is os.replace'd into the cache only when complete, so a crash never leaves a half-built model the readiness gate would mistake for a finished one.

Qwen3 prepare ends with verify_qwen3_session, which loads the converted weights and transcribes one second of silence — preparation used to end at 'files on disk', letting a bad conversion surface only during a real meeting, so the check moves that failure into the step whose job is to report it; it also warms the gated pyannote community-1 pipeline with the HF_TOKEN from the prepare environment.

refine requires GALPI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY in the environment and raises InvalidInput (exit 2) without it; it reads optional background text plus participants/glossary JSON into typed records (name/term required, InvalidInput otherwise), rendering empty or absent context as explicit placeholder blocks so the model relies on transcript evidence only.

The meeting date comes from --meeting-date, which the host derives from the source audio file's mtime (a recording is written when the meeting ends, so its timestamp is the meeting's day, unlike the transcript's); without the flag the worker falls back to the transcript file's own mtime, and the prompt pins the date unless the transcript carries explicit contradicting evidence.

Refinement routing is a pure length function: transcripts of 48,000 characters or fewer go through one streaming request; longer ones are split at whole speaker-turn boundaries into chunks of at most 16,000 characters, each carrying the last 400 characters of the previous chunk as a read-only <이전구간끝> preamble; map facts run with three concurrent workers and notes are reassembled in transcript order with progress reported per completed chunk; one reduce pass then composes the final document; progress stays monotonic on phase (map 35-68%, reduce 70-88%, single-pass streaming 35-88%).

minutes_template.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT is the single normative minutes format — status header, TL;DR, meeting purpose, decisions with content/evidence/impact/decider/status fields, action board, per-topic discussion, follow-ups, risks/open questions, and a correction appendix with confidence — with missing sections keeping their titles as 해당 없음, sensitive strings masked, and speaker labels never promoted to real names without evidence; both the single-pass prompt and the reduce prompt use this structure, keeping short and long meetings' minutes interchangeable.

assistant_stream.py's module-constant block is the source of truth for the assistant API defaults, which other code reads by name instead of restating the numbers: base URL from GALPI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL (default DEFAULT_BASE_URL, https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4), default model glm-5.3-flash, reasoning_effort included only when set to a value in REASONING_EFFORTS (low/medium/high/max), temperature 0.2, a 600-second request timeout, and GLM models on the default endpoint get 131072 max output tokens while everything else gets 32768.

The SSE consumer separates content from reasoning_content (while only reasoning has arrived, progress reports the live reasoning length at the band start), raises immediately on an error payload inside the stream, turns an empty document into an actionable error naming the finish reason (length and content_filter get Korean operator-facing messages), and strips a whole-document code fence before writing atomically and emitting the `refined` event.

The protocol envelope is mirrored in Rust: domain/worker.rs parses each stdout line into a WorkerEnvelope whose `v` must equal protocol version 1 and rejects other versions, which is why a protocol change (version, event names, fields) must update protocol.py, worker.rs, and the frontend event schema together — never Python alone.

The worker reads nearly all configuration from the host-built environment: HF_HOME/TORCH_HOME inside the app cache (which also determines where mlx_asr_model_dir resolves the converted weights), HF_TOKEN only during prepare for the gated pyannote model, telemetry opt-outs always set, GALPI_ASSISTANT_* variables for refine, locale pinned to ko_KR.UTF-8 with PYTHONUTF8=1, and PYTHONPATH at the worker root with PYTHONSAFEPATH=1.

Dependency pins are split per virtualenv — requirements.txt (whisperx 3.8.6, torch 2.8.0, torchaudio 2.8.0, pyannote.audio 4.0.7, imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0) and requirements-qwen3.txt (mlx-qwen3-asr[aligner] 0.3.5, mlx 0.32.1, torch kept only because pyannote imports torchaudio at module scope) — each with a resolved .lock the app installs from, regenerated with uv pip compile.

The worker's test suite deliberately excludes everything requiring the ML stack (real model loads, ASR quality, diarization behavior) and instead pins pure contracts: speaker hints, hotword packing, hallucination/loop filters against realistic Korean speech, SRT timestamp rounding, protocol stdout isolation, chunk-limit invariant, chunk planning, word-span segmentation, checkpoint cross-engine rejection, prompt/chunking rules, and SSE parsing.
